recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Future work should be based on new WG decisions about broadening Consent.subject target types or provider-directory profiling, not on FHIR-15112.
issue_request: FHIR-15112 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 CBCC change request asking to relax Consent.patient from 1..1 to 0..1 so Consent could be used for provider-directory restrictions without a required patient. Its resolution also proposed making Consent.scope extensible with invariants for existing patient-oriented scopes.
initial_application: The issue was applied historically in commit 2c05932185 (GF#15112 GF#15102), which changed the Consent spreadsheet so Consent.patient moved from 1..1 to 0..1 while remaining Reference(Patient).
additional_context: Current Consent source is no longer spreadsheet-driven. Consent is active in source/fhir.ini, which maps old Consent.patient to Consent.subject and old Consent.scope to Consent.category. Later Published Consent decisions renamed Consent.patient to Consent.subject, added Practitioner and ResearchSubject subject options, and eliminated Consent.scope in favor of flexible Consent.category and profiling/IG guardrails.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active Consent definition has Consent.subject with min 0 and max 1, and the provider restriction example remains representable without a subject. Reintroducing the original scope invariant idea would conflict with later Published FHIR-31903.

related_jiras.note: Co-applied in historical commit 2c05932185 but concerned identifier cardinality, not this Consent.patient decision.
Changed Consent.category extensibility around the same STU3 Consent codelist/invariant discussion.
Later Published issue requiring Consent.scope extensibility and patient-privacy naming before scope was removed.
Renamed Consent.patient to Consent.subject and added Practitioner, explaining the current successor element.
Added ResearchSubject as another Consent.subject target after the patient-to-subject rename.
Eliminated Consent.scope and core category/scope invariants, superseding the scope part of the FHIR-15112 resolution.

evidence_items.summary: Consent.subject is defined with min 0 and max 1 and supports Patient, Practitioner, ResearchSubject, and Group.
evidence_items.learned: The current successor of Consent.patient is optional, satisfying the cardinality portion of FHIR-15112.

evidence_items.summary: Consent actor/management elements allow HealthcareService and Organization, and the VHDir provider restriction example has no subject element.
